newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FORECAST - Consensus of Reserve Bank of NZ's MPS.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Consensus of Reserve Bank of NZ's MPS.

text.p: Following are economists' comments on and forecasts for the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's monetary policy statement (MPS), due on Tuesday, December 17.
Q) Do you expect the RBNZ to ease monetary conditions?

Nine out of 10 respondents said the Reserve Bank would not officially signal conditions any easier than where they are currently. Five qualified that by saying the bank would endorse the market-led easing that has occurred since a new National-NZ First coalition government was formed on Tuesday, December 10.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said the bank would ease monetary conditions by raising the daily settlement cash target to NZ$15 million from its current $5 million.
"(The RBNZ) will indicate comfort with current conditions via mix of assumption, inflation forecasts and comments they make." - National Bank of NZ
"We expect the RBNZ to sanction the recent moves in interest rates and exchange rates as an appropriate move to more neutral monetary policy settings." - Bancorp Treasury Services
"They will validate the easing that has occurred to date. Have insufficient information to move further just yet." - Garlick and Co.
"Conditions have already eased and are now consistent with the new inflation band." - Bank of New Zealand.
The central bank's inflation target has been widened to 0-3 percent from 0-2 percent under the hew centre-right coalition government between the National and New Zealand First parties.

Economists' predictions of RBNZ assumptions on the average level of the Trade-Weighted Index in the March 1997 quarter, the TWI's level of appreciation per annum from the March 1997 quarter, and the average level of 90-day bank bills in the March 1997 quarter.
* BTNZ said there would possibly be an assumed appreciation, and if so it would be around one percent.

** SBC Warburg specified that these forecasts are for updated RBNZ assumptions, based on the new 0-3 percent underlying inflation target band. Its forecasts based on the old 0-2 pct framework were 67.0 (TWI), 0 (TWI appreciation), and 9.0 pct (90-day bank bills).
Economists' forecasts for annual underlying inflation.
Q) Do you think the Reserve Bank will change its signalling methods in the next six months? If so, when and in what way?
Four economists said no, while two declined to answer.

Of the four who said yes, ASB Bank was not yet sure how the bank would change its signalling methods, and BNZ saw a move to setting an official cash rate. SBC Warburg said the change could be included in the MPS and would give a better idea of the trade-off between the TWI and 90-day interest rates. The National Bank said: "Only to the extent that it will reinforce the nature of the trade-off between interest and exchange rates, probably by quantifying the impact of each on inflation".
